lede.headline: Trump hands out science medals to tech's billionaires, hours after a visa crackdown
lede.dek: Elon Musk, Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang and Michael Dell got the White House treatment on Thursday. Hours earlier, the administration suspended Microsoft and other sponsors from a green-card program.

stories.headline: Trump gives Musk, Brin, Huang science medals at White House
stories.move: President Trump awarded the National Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang and AMD's Lisa Su at a Washington ceremony on Thursday, October 8. Michael Dell and Microsoft's Satya Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation instead. Trump called Musk "our modern-day Thomas Edison" and said, "Because of these people here, we will always be on top. No one else can compete with us." Hours before the ceremony, the administration suspended Microsoft and several other companies from the green-card sponsorship program.
stories.why: The honors double as a message that the administration wants to keep its biggest AI and chip players close, even as it tightens the visa pipeline many of the same companies rely on for talent.
stories.bear: A medal ceremony changes nothing about earnings, chip supply or visa policy; it's a photo opportunity timed to distract from the visa suspension announced the same morning.
stories.watch: Whether the Permanent Labor Certification suspension affecting Microsoft and Adobe expands to other sponsors.

stories.headline: US suspends Microsoft, Adobe from green-card visa program
stories.move: The Trump administration suspended Microsoft, Adobe and several other companies from the H-1B permanent labor certification (green-card sponsorship) process, citing fraud. Vice President JD Vance announced it on Thursday, October 8, saying the program "has become rife with fraud," and said he'd support eliminating the H-1B program altogether. Microsoft said it "look[s] forward to providing the Administration with additional information" and that it files H-1B petitions only for workers who meet the visa category's standards.
stories.why: Microsoft is Steve Ballmer's largest asset and a major part of Bill Gates's fortune; a prolonged freeze on skilled-worker sponsorship touches the hiring pipeline behind their stakes.
stories.bear: This hits sponsorship paperwork, not current staff or product roadmaps, and Microsoft says it's cooperating; the practical effect on the company may be small.
stories.watch: Whether the suspension is lifted after Microsoft's response, or whether more sponsors are added to the list.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs upgrades Palantir to Buy on sovereign AI demand
stories.move: Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral on Thursday, October 8, with a 12-month price target of $230, implying about 18% upside from Wednesday's close of $194.12. The call cites demand for sovereign AI, bespoke AI systems and Palantir's forward-deployed engineering model. Shares rose 1.8% to $197.53 Thursday, outperforming a falling market (the S&P 500 fell 0.47%, the Nasdaq fell 1.25%).
stories.why: Palantir is chairman and major shareholder Peter Thiel's biggest publicly traded position; a bullish turn from a major bank adds to the stock's case after a lagging year against the Nasdaq 100.
stories.bear: Palantir still trades at a rich multiple on revenue growth that has to keep accelerating; one upgrade doesn't resolve the valuation debate, and Zacks Research cut its own rating to Hold around the same time.
stories.watch: Palantir's next quarterly report for whether sovereign and government deals keep growing as fast as Borges expects.

stories.headline: Tesla's Shanghai factory posts its best month of 2026
stories.move: Tesla's Shanghai factory wholesaled 95,366 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in September, per CPCA data reported around October 8-9 — up 5% from 90,812 a year earlier and 10.7% from August, its best month of 2026. Exports rose 58.3% year over year to 30,529 vehicles while domestic deliveries fell 9.4% to roughly 64,800. Shanghai wholesaled 743,060 vehicles over the first nine months of 2026, up about 22.5% from the same period in 2025.
stories.why: Exports, not Chinese demand, drove the gain; Tesla has extended Model 3 and Model Y discounts in China through October 31 to keep domestic buyers coming.
stories.bear: Wholesale figures count cars leaving the factory, not retail deliveries, and domestic China demand is still falling even as exports mask it.
stories.watch: Whether October discounts revive domestic Chinese demand, and Tesla's Q3 earnings report.

stories.headline: Tesla renames 'Full Self-Driving' to 'Assisted Driving' in Europe
stories.move: Tesla began calling its "Full Self-Driving" feature "Tesla Assisted Driving" on its European websites, Reuters reported October 9. Pages in Slovakia, Germany, Spain and the Netherlands now redirect to the new name, after Germany's transport ministry said the old name was misleading since the system requires constant driver supervision. The US site still uses "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)." Sweden and Italy have also raised concerns about the name. An EU-wide approval vote has been pushed from October to at least December.
stories.why: Musk has called the software central to Tesla's future growth; clearing regulatory objections to the name is a step toward EU-wide approval, which the rebrand alone doesn't guarantee.
stories.bear: Changing a label doesn't change the underlying software or resolve the technical sticking points Germany and France are still testing for.
stories.watch: The EU-wide vote on the driver-assist software, now expected no earlier than December.

stories.headline: Meta blocks TikTok parent ByteDance's ads in seven countries
stories.move: Meta banned advertising from ByteDance, TikTok's parent, on Facebook and Instagram, effective Thursday, October 8, in the US, Canada, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Thailand and Vietnam. The ban also covers third-party ads directing users to TikTok or other ByteDance properties. A Meta spokesperson said, "We don't have to run ads from a competitor whose goal is to pull people off our apps." The move follows a August settlement in which Meta agreed to daily and nighttime usage limits for minors, after which Meta pressed TikTok to adopt similar limits; TikTok rejected Meta's ads calling for that.
stories.why: Meta is using ad-platform access, not just price or features, as a competitive weapon against its biggest short-form video rival.
stories.bear: The ban could invite antitrust scrutiny over a dominant platform denying a rival access to its ad network, and neither company has disclosed how much ad revenue is actually at stake.
stories.watch: Whether Meta extends the ban to more countries or TikTok challenges it.

stories.headline: Berkshire raises Lennar stake past 12% despite short-seller report
stories.move: Berkshire Hathaway bought about 2.4 million Lennar Class A shares and 15,028 Class B shares, worth roughly $192.6 million, on October 1 and 2, lifting its stake to about 28.43 million Class A and 568,028 Class B shares, per an SEC filing reported October 6. Lennar shares fell sharply after short-seller Hunterbrook published a report on Lennar's dealings with its Millrose Properties spinoff, which it said bought more than 700 Lennar homes for an estimated $200 million-plus, 356 of them in the final week of Lennar's third quarter.
stories.why: Berkshire kept buying into the stock even as a short-seller report and a weak housing market pressured the shares — a vote of confidence from the company's largest outside shareholder.
stories.bear: Berkshire's purchases predate the Hunterbrook report; it's unclear whether Buffett's team would buy at the same pace now, and mortgage rates near 7.3% are still a drag on homebuilders.
stories.watch: Lennar's next earnings report and any Berkshire 13F update on whether the buying continued through the Hunterbrook selloff.

stories.headline: Amazon explores $8 billion investor financing for Nvidia chips
stories.move: Amazon is in talks with outside investors over roughly $8 billion of financing built around its Nvidia chips, the Financial Times reported October 2. Under the plan, the chips would move into a special-purpose vehicle that raises money from investors, with Amazon leasing them back for its data centers. As of the report, no deal had been finalized and Amazon had not commented.
stories.why: The structure would let Amazon keep using the chips in AWS while shifting some of the capital cost off its own balance sheet, as its 2026 capex is expected to run around $220 billion.
stories.bear: Advanced AI chips depreciate fast — Bloomberg has flagged roughly a five-year replacement cycle — so outside investors in the vehicle would bear the risk that newer Nvidia generations erode the hardware's value before the financing is paid off.
stories.watch: Whether Amazon and its investors finalize the structure, and whether other hyperscalers adopt similar off-balance-sheet chip financing.

filings.change: Bought ~2.4M Lennar Class A and 15,028 Class B shares (~$192.6M) Oct 1-2, lifting its stake to roughly 29M shares and past the 10% SEC reporting threshold.

Dangote Refinery's IPO prospectus shows a $1.82 billion first-half-2026 profit after a $476 million loss for all of 2025, Reuters reported.
Nigeria's NNPC is set to supply Dangote Refinery eight cargoes of Nigerian crude plus one WTI Midland cargo in October, Reuters reported.
memo: A fast, cheap fix on labeling can defuse a regulatory fight without touching the product — Tesla's rename shows compliance theater can buy time.
A big, patient shareholder can keep buying through bad headlines that would sink a smaller holder's conviction — Berkshire's Lennar buying is a reminder that staying power is itself an edge.
Platforms are now treating ad-network access as a competitive weapon, not just a revenue line — expect more bans like Meta's on rivals, not fewer.
